scenes.visual: Title card 'Can It Grow When Rare?' fades in over two cartoon populations of small round creatures, one TEAL (#0e7c86) and one ORANGE (#e57200), nibbling from one shared seed pile. COLOUR MAP, same in both films, the text and the lesson's simulator: TEAL = species 1; ORANGE = species 2. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Creatures and room bars are cartoons labelled 'schematic'; the phase-plane lines and trajectories are computed from the Lotka-Volterra equations and labelled 'computed'.

scenes.tts: Two species eat the same limited food, and one grows twice as fast. Must the faster one win? This film builds the test that decides.
scenes.visual: The two populations side by side. A speedometer badge over TEAL reads 'growth rate x2' (as in the lesson's worked pair, where species 1 grows twice as fast). A large question mark appears over a podium labelled 'winner?' between them.
scenes.narration: Two species eat the same limited food, and one grows twice as fast. Must the faster one win? This film builds the test that decides.

scenes.tts: Start with the teal species alone. Its numbers rise toward its carrying capacity, big K, the size it settles at alone. Picture that capacity as a bar of room that fills up.
scenes.caption: Start with the teal species alone. Its numbers rise toward its carrying capacity, K, the size it settles at alone. Picture that capacity as a bar of room that fills up.
scenes.visual: ORANGE fades out. A horizontal bar labelled 'teal's room (K1)' appears. Each new TEAL creature that pops in drops one TEAL block into the bar; the bar fills from left toward a marker 'K1'. Beside it a small logistic S-curve draws itself (computed), levelling off at K1.
scenes.narration: Start with the teal species alone. Its numbers rise toward its carrying capacity, K, the size it settles at alone. Picture that capacity as a bar of room that fills up.

scenes.tts: As the room fills, growth per individual slows. That is the per-capita growth rate, and it reaches zero when the bar is full.
scenes.visual: A dial labelled 'per-capita growth rate' sits above the bar. As TEAL blocks fill the bar, the needle swings down from 'r1' (maximum) toward '0'; at a full bar the needle rests exactly on 0.
scenes.narration: As the room fills, growth per individual slows. That is the per-capita growth rate, and it reaches zero when the bar is full.

scenes.tts: Now bring back orange. Each orange individual takes some of teal's room too. A number called alpha says how much, counted in teal individuals.
scenes.visual: ORANGE creatures return. Each one drops a SMALLER ORANGE block into teal's room bar, next to the TEAL blocks; a label 'alpha12 = size of one orange block, in teal units' points at it. The dial needle drops a little with each orange block. Two sliders show 'small alpha: thin orange blocks' and 'large alpha: thick orange blocks'.
scenes.narration: Now bring back orange. Each orange individual takes some of teal's room too. A number called alpha says how much, counted in teal individuals.

scenes.tts: Read the two numbers after alpha as on, then from. Alpha one two is the effect on species one, from species two. Orange has its own room bar, filled the same way.
scenes.caption: Read the two numbers after alpha as on, then from. alpha12 is the effect on species 1, from species 2. Orange has its own room bar, filled the same way.
scenes.visual: On-screen text 'alpha12: ON species 1, FROM species 2' with an arrow ORANGE -> TEAL; then 'alpha21: ON species 2, FROM species 1' with an arrow TEAL -> ORANGE. A second bar 'orange's room (K2)' appears below the first, receiving ORANGE blocks and smaller TEAL blocks.
scenes.narration: Read the two numbers after alpha as on, then from. alpha12 is the effect on species 1, from species 2. Orange has its own room bar, filled the same way.

scenes.tts: Now plot both species at once. Teal numbers run across, and orange numbers run up. The teal line marks every mix where teal stops growing. On one side teal grows; on the other it shrinks.
scenes.visual: The bars slide away. Axes appear: x 'teal numbers (N1)', y 'orange numbers (N2)'. A straight TEAL line (computed) runs from a point on the x-axis marked 'K1' up to the y-axis. Small horizontal TEAL arrows below-left of it point right (teal grows); above-right of it they point left (teal shrinks). Label: 'teal isocline: teal growth = 0'.
scenes.narration: Now plot both species at once. Teal numbers run across, and orange numbers run up. The teal line marks every mix where teal stops growing. On one side teal grows; on the other it shrinks.

scenes.tts: That line is teal's isocline, its zero-growth line. Orange gets one too. Where the two isoclines cross, neither species changes. Is that crossing where they end up?
scenes.visual: A straight ORANGE line (computed) appears from 'K2' on the y-axis down to the x-axis, with small vertical ORANGE arrows (up below it, down above it). The two lines cross; a white ring marks the crossing, labelled 'neither changes'. A small '?' blinks beside the ring.
scenes.narration: That line is teal's isocline, its zero-growth line. Orange gets one too. Where the two isoclines cross, neither species changes. Is that crossing where they end up?

scenes.tts: Here is the test. Shrink teal to a few individuals, and let orange sit at its own carrying capacity. Can teal grow? This is the invasion test.
scenes.visual: A dot slides onto the y-axis at 'K2', then nudges a hair to the right: 'teal rare, orange at K2'. A spotlight on that dot. Card: 'invasion test: can a rare species grow when its competitor is at carrying capacity?'
scenes.narration: Here is the test. Shrink teal to a few individuals, and let orange sit at its own carrying capacity. Can teal grow? This is the invasion test.

scenes.tts: Here teal's arrow points away from zero, so rare teal grows. Swap roles, and rare orange grows too. Both pass. Every path that starts with both species present flows into the crossing. They coexist stably.
scenes.visual: At the spotlit dot a TEAL arrow points right: 'teal passes'. A second dot at 'K1' on the x-axis nudged slightly up shows an ORANGE arrow pointing up: 'orange passes'. Then six computed trajectories, each starting strictly inside the quadrant with both species present, curve into the white ring. One faint axial trajectory stays on the x-axis and runs to 'K1', labelled 'a species at zero stays at zero'. Stamp: 'both pass -> stable coexistence'.
scenes.narration: Here teal's arrow points away from zero, so rare teal grows. Swap roles, and rare orange grows too. Both pass. Every path that starts with both species present flows into the crossing. They coexist stably.

scenes.tts: Now make teal hurt orange more, so orange's line tilts. Rare orange, among a full teal population, now shrinks. Teal passes, orange fails, and orange slides to zero. Teal excludes it from this place.
scenes.visual: Animate alpha21 increasing (on-screen 'alpha21 up'): the ORANGE isocline swings until it lies entirely below the TEAL one, so they no longer cross. At the dot near 'K1' the ORANGE arrow now points DOWN: 'orange fails'. Computed trajectories all run to the point 'K1' on the x-axis; the ORANGE creatures fade from a small inset of the habitat. Stamp: 'one passes -> it excludes the other, here'.
scenes.narration: Now make teal hurt orange more, so orange's line tilts. Rare orange, among a full teal population, now shrinks. Teal passes, orange fails, and orange slides to zero. Teal excludes it from this place.

scenes.tts: Cross the lines the other way, and neither passes. Each species wins from some starts, so the starting numbers decide.
scenes.visual: Both isoclines are reset to cross with the ORANGE line steeper at the top and the TEAL line further out at the bottom (bistable arrangement, computed). Both rare-invader arrows point back toward the axes: 'neither passes'. Computed trajectories split: some run to 'K1' on the x-axis, some to 'K2' on the y-axis. A faint dashed curve between them is labelled 'dividing line (not equal numbers)'. Stamp: 'neither passes -> the start decides'.
scenes.narration: Cross the lines the other way, and neither passes. Each species wins from some starts, so the starting numbers decide.

scenes.tts: Back to the pair that coexist. Now double orange's growth rate, and change nothing else. Does the ending change?
scenes.visual: Reset to the coexistence picture with the white ring. The speedometer badge 'orange growth rate x2' flies onto ORANGE in a small inset. Trajectories are paused at their starts.
scenes.narration: Back to the pair that coexist. Now double orange's growth rate, and change nothing else. Does the ending change?

scenes.visual: Frozen frame. On-screen: 'Same ending, or a new one?' with a 5-second countdown ring.

scenes.tts: The ending stays put. Orange moves faster and the paths bend, but they still finish at the same crossing. Here, growth rate changes the route, not the outcome. So in this model, the faster grower need not win.
scenes.visual: Trajectories replay side by side: left panel 'original' (slow), right panel 'orange growth rate x2' (faster, more curved toward orange first) — both end in the same white ring (computed). Label: 'r changes speed and path, not the ending'. The isoclines do not move.
scenes.narration: The ending stays put. Orange moves faster and the paths bend, but they still finish at the same crossing. Here, growth rate changes the route, not the outcome. So in this model, the faster grower need not win.

scenes.tts: In words, each species must limit itself more than it limits the other. Limits means the share of each room that one individual fills.
scenes.visual: The two room bars return, drawn at different lengths (K1 longer than K2). One TEAL individual's share is highlighted on each: on teal's bar a sliver labelled '1/K1 of teal's room'; on orange's bar a sliver labelled 'alpha21/K2 of orange's room'. A comparison sign appears: '1/K1 > alpha21/K2'. Then the mirror comparison for one ORANGE individual: '1/K2 > alpha12/K1'. Text: 'each limits itself more than it limits the other'. Two check marks appear: 'teal passes', 'orange passes'.
scenes.narration: In words, each species must limit itself more than it limits the other. Limits means the share of each room that one individual fills.

scenes.tts: So the whole verdict comes from one question, asked of each species. Can it grow when rare, beside a competitor at full strength?
scenes.visual: The phase plane shrinks into a corner; three small icons line up: 'both pass: coexist', 'one passes: exclusion here', 'neither: start decides'. The question 'Can it grow when rare?' writes itself across the top.
scenes.narration: So the whole verdict comes from one question, asked of each species. Can it grow when rare, beside a competitor at full strength?

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot holding a small TEAL and ORANGE creature. Take-home line: 'In this model, both coexist stably when each can grow when rare.'
